warnings: Training source: completed POS ingredient consumption only; generated CSV is development-only; stock source: Historical daily inventory snapshot 2026-10-09.
Store operates daily, 1 PM–10 PM (Asia/Manila): SARIMA uses daily totals and seven-day seasonality, not hourly forecasts.
Product filters show store-wide ingredient demand, not predicted product sales.

SARIMA compares log1p and scaled raw usage, recent/full history, Philippine holidays and weekday effects. Selection targets period usage error within a 10% MAE guard and 10% MAPE/RMSE limits relative to the reference MAPE objective. Zeros remain in absolute errors; undefined percentage errors are null.

Daily intervals target 95% coverage with up to 12 calibration periods and five later test periods excluded from the earlier model selection. A positive-usage tail guard protects against spikes; fewer than 19 positive calibration samples use the observed maximum, not a validated 95% positive-demand quantile. Measured coverage is reported separately; daily bounds are not simultaneous weekly bounds.
Operational training: 365 covered POS days through 2026-10-06; generated CSV usage is excluded.

Portfolio-enabled ingredients use chronological method selection by daily and period absolute error, separate residual calibration, and a later promotion check. Older SARIMA-only selection and interval rules above apply to legacy or constant-history fallbacks. Portfolio promotion tests are not an untouched deployment holdout. Supplier facts and service-level targets require review.
Historical data ends 2026-10-06; forecasting bridges a 3-day gap.
Catalog identities, units and reorder points use raw-materials-and-products.csv; current stock uses the live snapshot. The catalog supplies no lead time or safety stock, so these default to zero.
Some legacy POS consumption records lack a unit snapshot. Their units are assumed from the catalog; incompatible current inventory units are excluded. Verify these units before relying on estimates.

Portfolio upgrade: chronological model selection, independent calibration windows, and later tests used by a promotion gate. Predictions are not actual POS sales. Supplier lead time and policy constraints require verification. Seeded observations do not establish real-world accuracy.
